2.w: “Listen carefully [to] my speech, and let this be your⁺ consolation.

3.w: Bear with me, and I will speak; and after I have spoken, you may mock.

4.w: As for me, is my complaint against man? And if [so], why [should] not my spirit be short?

5.w: Turn to me and be appalled, and put a hand over [your] mouth.

6.w: Even when I remember, then I am terrified, and trembling seizes my flesh.

7.w: Why do the wicked live on, growing old, even becoming mighty in power?

8.w: Their seed is established with them before their face, and their offspring before their eyes.

9.w: Their houses [are] safe from dread, and the rod of God is not upon them.

10.w: His bull passes over, without fail; his cow brings forth, and [does] not miscarry.

11.w: They send forth their little boys like a flock, and their children skip about.

12.w: They lift up to the tambourine and harp, and they rejoice at the sound of the flute.

13.w: They wear out their days in prosperity, and in peace go down to Sheol.

14.w: And they said to God, ‘Turn away from us! For we do not delight to know Your ways.

15.w: What [is] Shaddai that we should serve Him? And what do we gain that we should meet with Him?’

16.w: Behold, their own good [is] not in their hand; the counsel of the wicked is far from me.

17.w: How often [is] the lamp of the wicked put out, and their destruction comes upon them? The pains He apportions in His anger.

18.w: They become like straw before the face of the wind, and like chaff that the storm carries him away.

19.w: Does God store up for his sons his trouble? Let Him repay to him, and he will know.

20.w: Let his eyes see his destruction, and let him drink from the wrath of Shaddai.

21.w: For what [is] his delight in his house after him, when the number of his months is cut off?

22.w: Can one teach knowledge to God, since He judges those being high?

23.w: This one dies in the bone of his perfection, all of him at ease and at rest;

24.w: his pails are full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is moist.

25.w: And this one dies bitter in soul, and not having eaten of the good.

26.w: Together upon the dust they lie down, and the worm covers them over.

27.w: Behold, I know your⁺ thoughts, and the notions you⁺ wrest upon me.

28.w: For you⁺ say, ‘Where [is] the house of the noble? And where [is] the tent of the habitation of the wicked?’

29.w: Have you⁺ not asked those passing along the way, and do you⁺ not recognize their signs,

30.w: that from a day of calamity the evil one is held back, [and] in the day of wrath they are brought forth?

31.w: Who shall declare his way to his face? And who will repay him [for] what he has done?

32.w: When he is brought along to the graves, then one keeps watch over [his] tomb.

33.w: The clods of the torrent are sweet to him; and after him every man will extend, and those before his face are without number.

34.w: And how can you⁺ comfort me in vain, and in your⁺ answers remains falsehood?”
